react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the primary perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA (merged SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) ranks the five overlapping input compounds—sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), and galactitol (KEGG:C01697)—as significant hits in both Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052) with identical FDR of 1.06 × 10⁻¹³ and fold-enrichment of approximately 1,089. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently recovers the same KEGG map00052 pathway with p = 5.16 × 10⁻⁸ and five hit compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring returns MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 with p = 0.0063, covering 12 of its 13 pathway metabolites. The five driver metabolites are canonical members of SMPDB:SMP00043 and KEGG:map00052, verified through the metabolites_hit list returned by both RaMP and MetaboAnalystR. A secondary signal separates as the aspirin/paracetamol axis. REACT:R-HSA-9749641 (Aspirin ADME) is enriched with FDR = 1.82 × 10⁻⁴, and acetylsalicylate (CHEBI:13719) and paracetamol (CHEBI:46195) are overlapping hits in both the Aspirin ADME and Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1430728) pathways.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the primary perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA (merged SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) ranks the five overlapping input compounds—sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), and galactitol (KEGG:C01697)—as significant hits in both Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052) with identical FDR of 1.06 × 10⁻¹³ and fold-enrichment of approximately 1,089. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently recovers the same KEGG map00052 pathway with p = 5.16 × 10⁻⁸ and five hit compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scoring returns MUMM:galactose_metabolism at rank 4 with p = 0.0063, covering 12 of its 13 pathway metabolites. The five driver metabolites are canonical members of SMPDB:SMP00043 and KEGG:map00052, verified through the metabolites_hit list returned by both RaMP and MetaboAnalystR. A secondary signal separates as the aspirin/paracetamol axis. REACT:R-HSA-9749641 (Aspirin ADME) is enriched with FDR = 1.82 × 10⁻⁴, and acetylsalicylate (CHEBI:13719) and paracetamol (CHEBI:46195) are overlapping hits in both the Aspirin ADME and Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1430728) pathways.
